usageNotes: Returns a list of recent tasks cluster-wide, each represented by a UPID (Unique Process ID) string that encodes the node, task type, PID, and start time. Use this to discover in-progress or recently completed async operations across all nodes without needing per-node queries. No special privilege is required beyond a valid authenticated session.
tips: Each returned UPID can be decoded or passed to node-level task endpoints (e.g., GET /nodes/{node}/tasks/{upid}/status) to retrieve full status and log output.
The list is scoped to recent tasks; very old tasks may not appear — use node-level task history endpoints if you need historical data beyond the rolling window.
Because permissions are 'user: all', any authenticated API token can call this endpoint, but task log detail endpoints may enforce stricter per-task or per-node ACLs.
